submission.justification:
Based on comprehensive simulation studies, Absorber-F2 with 5 mm plate thickness provides the best energy resolution at 100 GeV among all tested configurations. The systematic evaluation showed:

1. Initial screening at 5 mm thickness across all three candidate materials revealed F2 achieved 3.239% resolution, significantly better than F1 (4.048%) and F3 (5.083%).

2. Thickness optimization for F2 was performed across the allowed range (2-10 mm), testing 2, 4, 5, 6, 8, and 10 mm plates. The 5 mm thickness yielded the optimal resolution of 3.239%, with performance degrading at both thinner (3.637% at 2mm) and thicker (4.369% at 10mm) configurations.

3. All three materials are mechanically compatible with the detector design and meet the hands-on maintenance requirement (verified through radiation safety documentation).

The recommended configuration of F2 at 5 mm thickness achieves the best possible energy resolution while satisfying all design constraints including the plate thickness range (2-10 mm) and hands-on maintenance accessibility during shutdowns.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible energy resolution at 100 GeV
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F2 at 5 mm achieves 3.239% resolution at 100 GeV, which is the best among all tested configurations including F1 (4.048% at 5mm), F3 (5.083% at 5mm), and all other F2 thicknesses tested (ranging from 3.239% to 4.369%).

requirements.requirement: The absorber must be one of the three materials listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F2 is one of the three candidate materials evaluated (F1, F2, F3). All three materials were confirmed mechanically compatible during document review.

requirements.requirement: The calorimeter must allow hands-on maintenance during shutdowns
requirements.evidence: Hands-on maintenance requirement was verified (hands_on_maintenance_verified = 1). All three candidate materials, including F2, were confirmed compatible with this requirement through radiation safety documentation review.

The recommended plate thickness of 5 mm falls within the required range of 2-10 mm. Thickness optimization included testing at 2, 4, 5, 6, 8, and 10 mm to ensure the optimum was found within constraints.
